analysis:
The PR routes the macOS jobs in ci.yml through the existing route job. Each provider and cluster shard gets its own lane, and the fallback stays blacksmith-12vcpu-macos-27. Visible head lines in ci.yml (1067-1217) show runs-on switched to fromJSON(needs.route.outputs.routes)[...] for test-cluster-gpu (1074) and test-cluster-focused (1136). Checkout, .git cache restore, git fsck discard and save steps are unchanged. persist-credentials stays false. Cache saves remain gated by SAVE_CACHES (master/dev pushes only), as in docs/developer/build.md CI Caching. The changelog and docs updates only describe this behavior. They remove the old 'not routed' paragraph, which cited performance data and a test, scripts/test-darkbloom-route.py, that asserted a literal Blacksmith label. That script is not supplied, so whether it was updated is unverified.

No provider, coordinator, attestation, key or cache-storage code changed, so TB-002, TB-011, A-001, A-003 and A-015 through A-017 are not touched. CI infrastructure is outside the provider threat model's in-scope list. The route job's security properties are described only in the docs, not shown: fork PRs are excluded, only exact Darkbloom labels are accepted, and the route job has no token permissions. They are unverified in the supplied source, and the route job's behavior when a lane is missing from the routes map is also unseen.

Residual questions for integration: whether Darkbloom macOS sandboxes run same-repo PR code with isolation from provider-operator Macs or add-on VMs (TB-012/TB-013), and whether the route workflow and its tests were updated consistently. Neither is evidenced as a regression here.
